nodes.title: How will this wallet be structured?
nodes.body:
**Educational presentation — not financial advice.**

Who holds the keys that authorize spending?

nodes.title: Which custody model?
nodes.body: A third party holds Bitcoin on your behalf. You hold an account claim — not necessarily on-chain keys.

nodes.title: Which custodian?
nodes.body: Pick a recognizable service. Icons are brand marks; offerings change — verify current features yourself.

nodes.title: How will you secure the Kraken account?
nodes.body: Baseline: **username + password**. Typically: TOTP, passkeys, hardware security keys; Global Settings Lock. SMS is weaker (SIM-swap).

nodes.title: How will you secure the Coinbase account?
nodes.body: Baseline: **username + password**. Typically TOTP / SMS / passkey-style MFA. SMS remains SIM-swap exposed.

nodes.title: How will you secure this Stacks-related account?
nodes.body: Auth varies by product. Treat like a common web custodian unless you verify otherwise.

nodes.title: How will you secure the Coinos account?
nodes.body: Web wallet with Lightning and custodial options. Confirm current 2FA in-product.

nodes.title: How will you secure the Bull Bitcoin account?
nodes.body: Exchange / buy-sell. Verify current MFA in-app.

nodes.title: How will you recover Wallet of Satoshi access?
nodes.body: Lightning custodial mode often uses **email-based** recovery rather than a BIP39 seed you control.

nodes.title: How will you secure the Bitcoin Well account?
nodes.body: Buy/sell and related services. Confirm MFA with the provider.

nodes.title: What remains on this custodial path?
nodes.body:
**Operable account claim** — auth hardening helps takeover risk; it does **not** remove counterparty risk (insolvency, freeze, seizure, KYC).

Apply paired mitigations above. Continue hardening below — or leave only if comparing structures.

nodes.title: Which federation style?
nodes.body: Operators jointly custody or mint claims. Trust: federation membership, threshold, and **your** seed/claim backup.

nodes.title: How will you back up your Fedi claim?
nodes.body: Community / federation custody. Vulns: guardian collusion, phishing of federation seeds, jurisdictional seizure, hard recovery if keys are lost.

nodes.title: How will you secure federated Lightning access?
nodes.body: Same core risks: **collusion**, phishing, concentrated jurisdiction, and seed/claim loss.

nodes.title: What remains on this federated path?
nodes.body: **Profile:** community trust instead of a single company; often better privacy UX. Residual: collusion, legal concentration, seed loss without exchange-style recovery.

nodes.title: Single key or multisignature?
nodes.body: You hold the keys. Structure matters: one key vs multisignature.

nodes.title: Which single-key tool?
nodes.body: Choose the device or software that will hold or sign with the key. Tool choice unlocks different seed, storage, and protection options.

nodes.title: How will you generate the Ledger seed?
nodes.body: Ledger creates BIP39 on-device. Prefer adding user entropy when available. Seed stays on device; optional passphrase.

nodes.title: PIN and passphrase on Ledger?
nodes.body: PIN protects the device. BIP39 passphrase creates a hidden wallet — backup separately and test recovery.

nodes.title: How will you generate the Trezor seed?
nodes.body: Trezor generates BIP39 on-device. Shamir (SLIP39) is an advanced option on some models — educational path sticks to BIP39.

nodes.title: PIN and passphrase on Trezor?
nodes.body: PIN on-device; optional passphrase. Verify firmware signatures on first use.

nodes.title: How will you generate the Coldcard seed?
nodes.body: Coldcard favors dice rolls and air-gapped ops (SD/QR). Seed can live on device or be wiped after backup.

nodes.title: Where will the Coldcard seed live?
nodes.body: Seed on device (PIN/passphrase), or ephemeral: backup to metal/SD then wipe for ultra-airgap posture.

nodes.title: How will Bitkey hold key material?
nodes.body: Bitkey uses a mobile + hardware collaborative design (typically 2-of-3). Cloud assist eases recovery — and reintroduces dependency.

nodes.title: Device PIN / app lock?
nodes.body: Protect the hardware and phone with strong PIN/biometrics; understand recovery paths before funding.

nodes.title: How will Seedsigner create entropy?
nodes.body: Seedsigner is typically **stateless**: generate, backup, sign via QR — seed not stored on device between sessions.

nodes.title: How will you store the Seedsigner backup?
nodes.body: No persistent seed on device means **your metal/paper backup is the wallet**. Geographic diversity matters.

nodes.title: How will you generate the Jade seed?
nodes.body: Blockstream Jade: on-device RNG, optional blind oracle for entropy assist, PIN, passphrase, BIP39 import.

nodes.title: PIN and passphrase on Jade?
nodes.body: PIN unlocks the device; passphrase optional. Prefer genuine purchase channel.

nodes.title: Which wallet tooling on Tails?
nodes.body: Tails is an amnesic live OS. **Electrum does not generate BIP39** — stay Electrum-native or use BIP39-capable offline tooling.

nodes.title: How will you keep Tails air-gapped?
nodes.body: Never "just enable Wi‑Fi" to install packages. Ferry verified software via USB.

nodes.title: Hot phone or move toward air-gap?
nodes.body: A normal smartphone wallet is **hot**. Malware, fake apps, and seed phishing dominate risk.

nodes.title: How will the phone create the seed?
nodes.body: App RNG is convenient. Avoid cloud screenshots and support that asks for seed words.

nodes.title: How will you back up the phone wallet?
nodes.body: Cloud backups of seeds are high risk. Prefer offline metal/paper; never screenshots.

nodes.title: How will you install signing software offline?
nodes.body: Air-gap fails when people break it to install apps. Use USB ferry of verified APKs; disable radios.

nodes.title: How will the air-gapped phone create the seed?
nodes.body: Generate BIP39 offline; write the seed; confirm restore produces the same first address.

nodes.title: Hot wallet or watch-only in BlueWallet?
nodes.body: BlueWallet can hold keys (hot) or import an xpub as watch-only. Lightning features may be custodial — check current mode.

nodes.title: How will BlueWallet get the seed?
nodes.body: App RNG or BIP39 import. Keep backups offline.

nodes.title: Descriptors or legacy wallet.dat?
nodes.body: Bitcoin Core on an online PC is a **hot** wallet unless the machine is dedicated/air-gapped. Prefer descriptor wallets.

nodes.title: Is this PC treated as hot or dedicated?
nodes.body: Online full node + wallet = hot malware surface. Dedicated offline machine changes the threat model.

nodes.title: How will you create physical entropy?
nodes.body: You generate first 11/23 words; compute checksum offline; load into a signing device.

nodes.title: How will multisig keys be distributed?
nodes.body: **m-of-n** keys to spend. Independence is the point: same-vendor or same-country stacks correlate risk.

nodes.title: Accept same-country risk or diversify?
nodes.body: Same-country stacks share **legal jurisdiction**, local disaster correlation, and easier coercion. Prefer geographic diversity when stakes warrant it.

nodes.title: Switch away from same-vendor multisig?
nodes.body: If all signers share firmware, RNG, and supply chain, **one vendor bug can hit your threshold**. Prefer multi-vendor.

nodes.title: Also distribute keys geographically?
nodes.body: Distinct manufacturers, purchase channels, and entropy sources. Export and backup the **wallet descriptor**.

nodes.title: Add independent human parties?
nodes.body: Keys in **different locations**. Still ensure you can assemble *m* keys when you need to spend or rotate.

nodes.title: Peer humans or a collaborative-custody firm?
nodes.body: Co-signers: spouse, attorney, firm, friend. Pros: inheritance & travel. Cons: collusion; a co-sign **service** can become custodian-like.

nodes.title: Can you still spend if the firm disappears?
nodes.body: Keep *m* such that you can still spend if the firm vanishes (e.g. 2-of-3 where you hold 2).

choices.label: No — firm is required to spend

nodes.title: Will you practice a recovery drill?
nodes.body: Document legal/practical expectations; practice recovery with a **test** wallet first.

nodes.title: What will you back up for multisig?
nodes.body: Backup **each seed**, the **descriptor**, derivation paths, and a written recovery playbook. Test restore with a tiny amount first.

nodes.title: What remains on this multisig path?
nodes.body: **Profile:** higher security against single theft/loss; complexity rises. Independence (vendors, locations, people) is the point.

nodes.title: Accept Glacier-style complexity?
nodes.body: Dual permanently offline computers, dice entropy, printed checklists. Highest single-org assurance — human error dominates residual risk.

nodes.title: Ready to run the ceremony outline?
nodes.body: Two air-gapped machines; dice → BIP39; checksum offline; dual-verify addresses; metal backup; inheritance sealed. Practice with **throwaway** entropy first.

nodes.title: What remains on this Glacier-style path?
nodes.body: **Profile:** maximum procedural security, minimum convenience. Best for infrequent-move cold storage when discipline is maintained.

nodes.title: Which dice procedure will you follow?
nodes.body: Casino/tested dice + trusted table; **never sort** multi-die outcomes before mapping.

choices.label: Casino dice + trusted table + no sorting

nodes.title: Will you use a reviewed card procedure?
nodes.body: Thorough shuffle + unbiased mapping. Use a **reviewed** guide; do math on paper.

nodes.title: Will you enforce ceremony OPSEC?
nodes.body: Pencil/paper only for intermediate math; never speak the seed; no cameras.

nodes.title: Where will you compute the checksum word?
nodes.body: BIP39's final word encodes a checksum. Wrong CLI, broken air-gap, or derivation mismatch can ruin recoverability.

nodes.title: What do you need before serious funds?
nodes.body: Restore-test backup; confirm identical addresses; export xpub to watch-only; decide passphrase, geographic backups, inheritance.

nodes.title: How will you export the xpub?
nodes.body: An **xpub** enables watch-only receive addresses without spending keys. Verify addresses on the cold/signing screen.

nodes.title: Will you verify receives on a cold device?
nodes.body: Phone can leak xpub (privacy) and display attacker-controlled addresses.

nodes.title: Do watch-only and device addresses match?
nodes.body: Export via QR or USB. Match address #0 with the hardware display.

nodes.title: Do offline and watcher addresses match?
nodes.body: If they disagree, stop — derivation mismatch or malware.

nodes.title: What next after watch-only is ready?
nodes.body: Monitor balances online without exposing spending keys. Treat the xpub as sensitive.

nodes.title: Which backup concern first?
nodes.body: Physical theft, fire/flood, and unclear inheritance destroy more coins than clever cryptography.

nodes.title: Which physical backup posture?
nodes.body: Stamp seeds into metal; avoid single points of disaster; consider tamper-evident bags.

nodes.title: Will you write an inheritance playbook?
nodes.body: Heirs need where materials are, software/paths, passphrase existence — **without** pasting the seed into a public will.

nodes.title: What next after backup posture improves?
nodes.body: Recoverability is up. Re-test restores periodically — especially after software upgrades.

nodes.title: Will you use a BIP39 passphrase?
nodes.body: Optional passphrase creates a hidden wallet. Great for secrecy — catastrophic if lost or untested.

nodes.title: Will you always verify on the signing device?
nodes.body: Malware can poison addresses; fake support asks for seeds; wrong derivation sends coins away.

choices.label: Yes — verify full address on device

nodes.title: What next after signing hygiene?
nodes.body: Combine with multisig if amounts warrant. Prefer staying on summary to apply remaining mitigations.

nodes.title: What remains on this self-custody path?
nodes.body: If keys are in place, the setup can operate — **risks may still remain**. Apply paired mitigations; continue hardening below rather than restarting the tree.
